title: introduce-premerge-viability-check-and-dep-safety-gate
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a premerge viability gate and integrates a dependency-safety check into CI; refactors lint/test runners to avoid duplicate work; small repo hygiene cleanups.
description:
Context and motivation: builds on ENG-9472 to further reduce wasted CI cycles and prevent unsafe dependency upgrades reaching main. We observed repeated flaps where dependabot PRs passed unit tests but caused flaky integration test reruns and occasional broken releases. This PR introduces a premerge viability check that runs a lightweight, deterministic set of validations and a dep-safety gate for automated dependency updates.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new GitHub Action 'premerge-viability' that runs early in the PR lifecycle; it performs quick static checks, a minimal lint (fast mode), and a targeted smoke test matrix against a pinned integration fixture. The intent is to fail fast and avoid starting heavy integration shards.
- Integrates a dependency-safety check (based on the internal dep-curator script) that verifies pinned transitive deps, checks for removed exports via a small static analyzer, and blocks merges from dependabot if risk > low.
- Refactors CI workflows so linters and typechecks are run as composite actions (python/ts), de-duplicating setup and reducing avg CI wall time for multi-language changes.
- Introduces a lightweight 'ci-dedupe' manifest that prevents duplicate test suites across staged lanes (fast feedback lanes will no longer start redundant integration shards already reserved for nightly runs).
- Small repo hygiene changes: cleans stale .gitignore entries, normalizes pre-commit hooks, and enforces 'signed-commits' for release-* branches via branch protection config snippets in workflows.

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): add premerge-viability action and workflow (aisha)
- feat(dep): dep-safety integration + risk scoring hook (aisha)
- refactor(ci): convert python/ts linters to composite actions and consolidate setup steps (chen)
- chore(repo): tidy .gitignore and pre-commit config (sofia)
- fix(ci): dedupe test lanes and add manifest-based guard (aisha)

Changed areas / files (high-level):
- .github/workflows/premerge-viability.yaml (new)
- .github/actions/composite/fast-lint-action/action.yml (new/refactor)
- .github/actions/dep-safety-check/run.sh (new)
- .github/workflows/ci-staged-lanes.yaml (modified)
- infra/ci/ci-dedupe-manifest.yaml (new)
- tools/dep-curator/score.py (modified)
- scripts/release/generate-draft.sh (small tweak to emit draft metadata)
- package.json, pyproject.toml (pin cleanup hints)

Notable implementation details:
- premerge-viability is intentionally conservative: it uses short timeouts and a small prebuilt fixture image so it remains cheap. The action matrix runs against node/python runtimes we support and returns a structured status (ok/warn/fail). The action emits annotations to the PR and adds a status check named 'premerge/viability'.
- dep-safety-check computes a heuristic risk score (0-100) using: semantic version delta, changed export set size, downstream usage count (best-effort), and a small AST diff to detect deleted/renamed exports. The threshold for blocking dependabot is configurable via repo-level .dep-safety.yaml. Example config: "block_threshold: 30".
- Composite lint actions factor out expensive language setup (toolchain install/caching) so multiple lint jobs in a matrix share cached toolchains and avoid repeated installs. The composite action also surfaces a 'fast' mode which runs a subset of linters when the PR touches <= 10 files.
- ci-dedupe-manifest is a human-editable YAML file that enumerates canonical shards; the workflow uses it to short-circuit duplicate shard launches. This prevents two workflows from booting the same heavy integration job.

Review conversation (summary):
- Liam O'Connor: requested tighter timeouts on the premerge fixtures and an explicit opt-out label for long-running test PRs. Action: added 'ci/skip-fastpath' label handling.
- Chen Wei: asked for metrics exports from the dep-safety-check (histogram of scores). Action: added a minimal Prometheus push gateway report and a trace id in the action logs.
- Sofia Martinez: flagged the release script change and requested compatibility with our changelog generator. Action: release/generate-draft.sh was updated to include changelog fragments and to create annotated draft release instead of auto-publishing.
- Security review (brief): verified that dep-safety runs in a read-only sandbox and that any credentials used for downstream heuristics are optional and default to offline heuristics.
- Author replies: updated timeouts, added metrics, documented opt-out label and .dep-safety.yaml, wrote unit tests for the risk scorer.

CI and testing:
- Local unit tests: pass (new unit tests for score.py).
- GitHub Actions: premerge and main CI lanes passed on the final run. Notable transient failure during iteration: flakiness in the old integration shard that motivated the ci-dedupe guard; fixed by dedupe manifest and a backoff in the scheduler.

Risk and rollout plan:
- Feature toggles are used: premerge-viability is enabled for selected repos only via .github/enable-premerge.yaml. We will enable for core repos for 2 weeks then roll org-wide.
- Dep-safety default is non-blocking for human-authored PRs; it is blocking only for dependabot/automated update PRs initially.

Merge outcome: squash and merge. Changelog entry created under 'ci improvements' with a short summary and rollout notes.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-9601: expand risk heuristics with runtime test coverage mapping.
- ENG-9622: dashboard for premerge-viability pass/fail trends and dep-safety scores.

If you want to test locally: see tools/dep-curator/README.md (includes a small docker-compose fixture used by the premerge action) and run: 
- ./tools/dep-curator/score.py --old-rev HEAD~1 --new-rev HEAD --output json
- act -P ubuntu-latest=nektos/act-environments-ubuntu:18.04 -j premerge-viability

Thanks to Chen and Sofia for the review and to infra for help with action runner quotas.
